author: Mark Atwood
text:
Survey complete.

Cross-references verified clean (no drift):
- urn:ietf:params:jmap:chat:websocket capability URN registered consistently in capabilities table and IANA section
- dataTypes list for state-change push (lines 123-131): exactly the 9 top-level data types with /changes methods in the main draft (ChatContact, Chat, Message, Space, ReadPosition, PresenceStatus, CustomEmoji, SpaceInvite, SpaceBan); 11 subtypes correctly omitted
- receiveTypingIndicators check (line 214, 375) consistent with main draft :450, :928 — direct/group only, channel exempt
- ChatTypingEvent rate limit 3s/sender/chat (line 212) consistent with main draft Chat/typing rate limit (:930) and federation Peer/typing rate limit (:393-395)
- ChatPresenceEvent rate limit 30s/contact (line 251) consistent with federation Peer/presence rate limit (:533)
- ChatPresenceEvent blocked-contact suppression (line 253, 376) consistent with main draft :354 ChatContact.blocked
- ownerUserId terminology (line 105) matches main draft :177 Session extension field
- Authentication strengthening of RFC 8887 4.2 MAY to MUST (line 107) is deliberate and rationalized in-text
- Authorization model (lines 370-384) is wire-level delivery rules, not Space-permission gated; recent commits c93e545, 9344aec, 38055ec, 970bad6 do not affect it

Findings filed:
- dim0 (P2 bug): WSS draft missing blocked-sender suppression for ChatTypingEvent. The WSS guide (:52) tells clients this happens; the draft does not normatively require it. Asymmetric vs ChatPresenceEvent which DOES have the rule. Privacy regression for a blocked user who can still send typing signals.
- ncnd (P4 editorial): line 113 method enumeration includes redundant ReadPosition/set (covered by /set) but omits Chat/typing (also non-CRUD shape); inconsistent singling-out.

Items considered and rejected as findings:
- 'Visibility' suppression mentioned in WSS guide :59 ('The recipient no longer has visibility of the contact'): forward-looking guidance, no specific spec mechanism it maps to; not actionable
- Hardcoded 3s typing and 30s presence rate limits: already tracked under uy1m (overdetermination, federation draft) and ic5s T3-2 (main draft rationale). WSS values are consistent with the existing hardcoding; the draft would update in parallel when those Tier 2/3 fixes land.
- 1008 close-frame status code on credential expiry (:107): deliberately strengthened from RFC 8887 MAY to MUST with rationale; not overdetermined in the problematic sense.
- 'maxConcurrentRequests' and 'pushState' references: correctly reference RFC 8887 sections; no drift.

bd remembered (separately) the typing-suppression privacy property as worth checking elsewhere if similar event-delivery features are added later.
